findings.title: Login cache invalidation is skipped for IDPs whose organization is disabled, leaving stale entries after the org is re-enabled
findings.body: registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate compares getLoginPredicate() on the 'original' and 'updated' models to decide whether the .idp.login caches must be invalidated. The 'original' model comes from getById() (line 91), which returns the organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() returns false whenever the linked organization is disabled. The cached login ID sets, however, are built from the JPA query which only looks at the raw flags (enabled, hideOnLogin, linkOnly, BROKER_PUBLIC). So an org-linked IDP with enabled=true in a disabled org IS present in the cached login sets, yet predicate(original) is false. If an admin then updates that IDP so it no longer qualifies for login (sets hideOnLogin=true, linkOnly=true, or BROKER_PUBLIC=false, or moves it to another org), predicate(updated) is also false and no invalidation is registered (the early return at line 405-407). When the organization is later re-enabled (an org update does not invalidate these caches), the stale cached ID set is served: getById returns the fresh model whose org-aware isEnabled() is now true, and the only consumer-side re-check added in this PR (OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean) filters on isEnabled() only, so an IDP that should be hidden, link-only, or private to an org is displayed on the login page. The predicate for the 'original' state should be evaluated against the unwrapped/raw stored model (as remove() already does with idpDelegate.getByAlias) so the comparison matches what is actually in the cache.

findings.title: Cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin registers removal of a literal IdP named "alias" instead of the created providers
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the creation loop does getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) with the literal string "alias" (same again at line 425 for idp-alias-20). No identity provider with alias "alias" exists, so the 21 providers the test creates (idp-alias-0 .. idp-alias-20, ten of them linked to orga) are never cleaned up, and the deferred remove() call will hit a 404 during cleanup. Because the test realm is shared across the class, the leftover org-linked IDPs contaminate other tests that assert exact counts — e.g. testCacheIDPByOrg asserts orga's cached IDP list has exactly 6 entries, which fails if testCacheIDPForLogin ran first and left 10 more IDPs linked to orga. The cleanup should reference the actual alias created in each iteration (and "idp-alias-20" for the later one), e.g. by capturing final String alias = "idp-alias-" + i and using get(alias).
